x1_execution_negatives.observed: The first read-only source-and-proposal inventory helper used the newer PowerShell null-coalescing operator, which the host Windows PowerShell parser rejected.
x1_execution_negatives.resolution: Rerun the same read-only inspection with an explicit null test; the 160-record inventory then completed without repository mutation.

x1_execution_negatives.observed: The draft x1 validation receipt predicted 33 checks before the exact-file-set and final privacy assertions were included; the complete checker reported 35.
x1_execution_negatives.resolution: Correct the receipt to 35 of 35 before commit and retain the pre-commit bookkeeping mismatch rather than erasing it.

x1_execution_negatives.observed: The first multi-file correction patch used an invalid hunk separator and was rejected atomically before changing any file.
x1_execution_negatives.resolution: Use valid separate update hunks for each file, reapply the correction, and retain the rejected patch as execution evidence.

x1_execution_negatives.observed: The first staged-name-hash receipt patch incorrectly placed a second file header inside an update hunk and was rejected atomically before changing any file.
x1_execution_negatives.resolution: Apply one valid update hunk per file, restage the complete packet, and retain the rejected patch as execution evidence.

x1_execution_negatives.observed: The first independent staged-name validation used the newer static SHA256.HashData API, which is unavailable in the host Windows PowerShell runtime.
x1_execution_negatives.resolution: Rerun the read-only hash check with SHA256.Create().ComputeHash, which is compatible with this host, and retain the rejected invocation.

x1_execution_negatives.observed: An overbroad OpenAI-style-secret regex matched the public suffix of two inherited risk-governor skill slugs inside the generated family index.
x1_execution_negatives.resolution: Require a non-slug token boundary before the secret prefix, rerun the scan, and retain the false-positive detector result rather than weakening the protected-content boundary.

review_conclusion: All ten proposals are distinct in operative mechanism from the 160 inherited records. Shared domain nouns remain because scientific, identity, authority, privacy, accessibility, and Stage 20 boundaries are intentionally preserved.
boundary: A collision audit supports workflow preregistration novelty only; it does not establish scientific novelty, patentability, publication priority, or empirical validity.
